items.desc: Young people in Germany will take to the streets this weekend to demand education and action on climate change. Politicians warn that the protests could become violent, as in France, but the situations are different.

items.title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than 80% of votes counted
items.titleOrig: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than 80% of votes counted
items.desc: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu bloc ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the final tally could take days. Neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.

items.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
items.titleOrig: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
items.desc: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

items.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
items.titleOrig: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
items.desc: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

items.title: Germany news: Parties debate who should succeed President Steinmeier, with several women under discussion
items.titleOrig: Germany news: Parties debate who should succeed President Steinmeier, with several women under discussion
items.desc: Germany's political parties are weighing possible successors to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, with no candidate agreed yet. Meanwhile, a poll suggests most Germans are giving Halloween a miss this year.

items.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
items.titleOrig: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
items.desc: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

items.title: Dozens of people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
items.titleOrig: Dozens of people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
items.desc: At least 68 people have been killed in a train crash in central Spain, local authorities have confirmed. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

items.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
items.titleOrig: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
items.desc: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

items.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
items.titleOrig: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
items.desc: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

items.title: India news: Cyclone Arnab turns deadly after landfall
items.titleOrig: India news: Cyclone Arnab turns deadly after landfall
items.desc: Cyclone Arnab killed at least three people in Andhra Pradesh after making landfall earlier today. Also, a new report says India is paying a steep economic cost over heat. Follow live.

items.title: Experts urge 'global health emergency' as climate harms accelerate
items.titleOrig: Experts urge 'global health emergency' as climate harms accelerate
items.desc: A new Lancet report reveals the growing toll of climate change on human health, from rising heat deaths and drought to food insecurity and lost livelihoods.

items.titleOrig: Egypt orders closure of independent news site Mada Masr
items.desc: Editor-in-chief Lina Attalah was briefly detained and fined over licensing violations. Rights groups condemned the ruling as a major blow to press freedom in Egypt, where independent media face growing pressure.
